item.title: Wife's support during husband's medical training becomes key in divorce asset battle
item.description: An Alabama appeals court reversed a divorce property settlement after finding that a lower court wrongly excluded a surgeon's medical-business interests, acquired during his marriage, from marital assets. His wife had supported the household while he completed medical training. The case has been sent back for a fresh valuation and division of the couple's property.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Prince William may let daughter Charlotte give up royal titles; 11-year-old dreams of stage career
item.description: Princess Charlotte could pursue a career in the performing arts, with reports suggesting she dreams of becoming an actress or singer. Prince William may reportedly allow his younger children to give up their royal titles and HRH styles when they become adults, giving Charlotte and Prince Louis the freedom to choose independent careers away from royal duties.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: A monarch butterfly named Lulu, wearing a tag, flew about 600 miles from Idaho to California
item.description: Lulu, a monarch butterfly, is currently migrating from Idaho to California, equipped with a Bluetooth tag that allows researchers to track her journey. This migration emphasizes the critical decline of western monarch populations linked to environmental issues. To aid conservation, the Ellwood Friends group has launched a fundraising campaign to name these tagged butterflies. In total, ten butterflies have been released to gather data on their migration routes.

item.title: California police officer pulls 18-year-old from burning Mercedes after train collision; bodycam captures rescue
item.description: An 18-year-old driver was trapped in a burning Mercedes-Benz after a collision with an Amtrak train. Police officers quickly arrived at the scene and pulled the unconscious driver from the wreckage. The rescue was completed in less than a minute, despite the risk of explosion. Firefighters worked to control the flames while medical personnel transported the driver to a local hospital.

item.title: At 91, Maeve McVeigh sinks 127-Yard hole-in-one, her second Ace since taking up golf at age 68
item.description: Maeve McVeigh, a spirited 91-year-old golfer from Northern Ireland, achieved her second remarkable hole-in-one at Dungannon Golf Club. This stunning feat, accomplished during a ladies' winter league match, saw her send the ball 127 yards directly into the hole. Unaware of her accomplishment until a friend prompted her to check, McVeigh exemplifies how women are increasingly embracing golf and forming connections in their community.

item.title: North Carolina farmer Noah Ranells has permanently protected 63 acres of his farm
item.description: Noah Ranells has taken a significant step by permanently conserving 63 acres of Fickle Creek Farm in Alamance County, North Carolina. This proactive move comes after a concerning decline in local farmland over the past decade. The farm is dedicated to producing meat, eggs, and vegetables for its community, ensuring a robust connection to local food sources.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In the late 1800s, drainage and a new river channel altered Florida's Ocklawaha Prairie
item.description: The Ocklawaha Prairie Restoration Area spans 6,301 acres in Florida, focused on revitalizing wetlands and promoting wildlife habitats. Key restoration efforts have led to improved water quality and increased capacity for floodwater storage. Complementing these efforts is a Chornobyl Memorial Forest honoring victims of the 1986 nuclear disaster. Visitors can enjoy hiking, fishing, and primitive camping, while seasonal waterfowl hunting adds to the area's recreational appeal.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Neighbours' safety fears put 100-acre Kansas deer-hunting business under zoning rules
item.description: A Kansas appeals court has ruled that a 100-acre deer-hunting business run by a couple cannot be treated as an agricultural operation and must obtain a special-use zoning permit. The ruling followed objections from two neighbouring couples, who raised safety concerns about commercial hunting taking place close to their properties.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Titanic survivor Lucy, Lady Duff Gordon’s diamond ring sells for £150,000 after staying in family for generations
item.description: A diamond ring belonging to Titanic survivor Lucy, Lady Duff Gordon, sold for £150,000 at auction. The ring was expected to fetch around £80,000 but achieved a much higher final price. Lady Duff Gordon wore the ring during the sinking of the Titanic, which occurred in 1912. Other Titanic memorabilia, including a rare ticket and a postcard, were also sold at the auction.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Wisconsin’s $1.1M Barbie Dream House goes under contract
item.description: In Hudson, Wisconsin, a charming pink Victorian house constructed in 1900 has made a remarkable transformation from its original Goth style. Recently listed at $1.1 million, the property is now under contract. Featuring seven bedrooms and four bathrooms, the home boasts inviting spaces for gatherings and rentals. The creative homeowner painted it pink and opened it up for various uses, showcasing its versatility.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Historic gold dredging damaged a California river used by salmon and steelhead
item.description: Major funding has been secured for restoration initiatives aimed at revitalizing the salmon habitat along the Tuolumne River. The project will reestablish 20 acres at La Grange, improving conditions for salmon and steelhead. With new side channels and a historic floodplain, the area will become conducive for salmon spawning. Collaborative efforts by various organizations since 2020 highlight an ongoing dedication to ecological preservation in this region.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Phoenix man's 2015 deed had wrong address; court upheld invalidation of rival deeds
item.description: A property dispute arose in Phoenix, Arizona, due to a mistake in a property's street address. Robert Olsen received a quitclaim deed from his father, which included incorrect address details but correct property descriptions. Bonitas Casitas LLC later claimed ownership and filed a lawsuit, leading to competing claims over the property. The Arizona Court of Appeals upheld the lower court's ruling, reaffirming the validity of Olsen's original deed.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Chef Jose Andres rescues Baltimore's 45-year-old Thanksgiving food tradition
item.description: Cynthia Brooks' efforts to continue her mother Bea Gaddy's 45-year-old Thanksgiving food tradition in Baltimore faced a setback after donations fell short, leaving her with only eight turkeys days before the event. Celebrity chef Jose Andres World Central Kitchen and the Maryland Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services stepped in with food and resources, helping save the annual dinner that began in 1981.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Marshall’s 700 Meals: Family keeps holiday dinners going; her home serves hundreds in need
item.description: Carolyn Marshall honors her late mother, Reverend Annie Woodridge, by preparing festive meals for those in need. Overcoming various obstacles, she turned her home into a hub for food prep, drawing support from volunteers who help package and deliver meals. This initiative has blossomed into a cherished family and community effort, reinforcing the values of kindness and remembrance associated with her mother's legacy during the holidays.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Adirondack Mountain Rescue: Becky’s arrival triggered search; rescuers found owner alive
item.description: When a basset hound named Becky showed up unaccompanied at a mountain lodge, it triggered an urgent search for her owner, a 69-year-old man living with dementia. Spending a night in the frigid wilderness, he was finally located by a hunter. Thanks to Becky's unexpected arrival, the rescue effort commenced quickly, potentially saving her owner's life.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk
